details:
WHAT IT IS

Aap Ka Khet (https://aapkakhet.readhaven.online/) helps smallholder farmers in Punjab choose their next crop rotation. A farmer enters their farm once — location, current crops, acres, water source, soil test, and their own mandi prices — and gets a Today advice page, a field view with a 3D/2D map and season timeline, and a rotation planner that compares their current rotation against five diverse alternatives, each with labelled Evidence, Benefits, Information gaps and Risks. Everything is in Urdu and English, written in plain language with a glossary for terms like NDVI, evapotranspiration and soil-moisture anomaly, and every recommendation carries the disclaimer to check with a local agriculture officer — the tool supports the farmer's decision, it does not take it from them.

WHY IT MATTERS

One heatwave or a waterlogged field can wipe out a season's income for a family farming 5 acres. Most advice tools assume literacy, English, and reliable internet. Aap Ka Khet is built for the farmer who has a phone, a small rain-fed or irrigated plot, and no agronomist on call.

WORKED EXAMPLE (VERIFIED ON THE LIVE APP)

A 5-acre rain-fed farm in Faisalabad growing Cotton→Wheat has a normal year worth about Rs 7.3 lakh. A drought could cost Rs 3.3 lakh — 46% of the year's harvest. The planner scores the farmer's current rotation 69.0 and offers five alternatives scoring up to 76.1, each with its evidence, gaps and risks, so the farmer can see exactly what changes and why. The app was tested on a real phone (Lahore farm, Sorghum→Berseem, 3 acres) with consistent numbers across pages, and loads in 2–3 seconds.

USE OF NASA DATA

NASA POWER provides the weather history and outlook shown on the Today page (latest data 11 Nov 2026). SMAP Level 4 provides root-zone soil moisture (0.16 in Faisalabad, 0.13 in Multan, dated 10 Nov 2026), shown with its source and date on the soil pages. MODIS and EONET are named in the app's sources; NDVI in the app is simulated and is labelled simulated — it is not presented as a real observation. Climate outlooks to 2041–2050 use WorldClim projections; per-crop labels show the real deltas (for example wheat heat-limit days 55→62, water need 450→462mm). Evidence links in the app currently go to source homepages rather than dataset-specific pages. No Space Agency Partner data was used.

AI USE (SUPER INTELLIGENCE)

Claude Code, an AI coding assistant, helped build and fix the app during the hackathon, and made the demo video; the video's voiceover is AI-generated and is disclosed as such on screen. All data claims in the app and in this submission were verified against the live app and the cited NASA sources. The Super Intelligence options selected in this form reflect the same use.

NEXT STEP

A pilot with smallholder farmers in Punjab to validate the advice against real fields and harvests. No real farmer has tested the app yet, and this submission does not claim otherwise.

CODE (PUBLIC)

Front end: https://github.com/Aqeel0317/nasa_challenge_front

Back end: https://github.com/Aqeel0317/nasa_backend
